summary: When the project has an approved Process Policy, `delivery_compile.py approve-scope` pins its path, revision and source hash in `delivery.md`, inside the scope hash, so each Delivery names the process switch values it ran under; a draft or invalid policy refuses scope approval. Without a policy nothing is pinned, the Delivery runs with every switch at its default, and a golden all-default run proves every Delivery compiler output byte-identical to the previous release on the same inputs apart from #322's `superseded_plan_approvals` in `execution-plan.md`. The pin is compared by value while an execution approval can still re-pin it, on the switches the Delivery still reads: for a scope-approved Delivery every switch a Delivery flow owns, and for an execution-approved one only those its `delivery-execution` flow owns, `execution_planning`, `implementation_schedule`, `owner_gates` and `review_loop`, since the next execution approval pins the planning switches anew. An approved policy that changes one of those values makes `check` and the coordinator verbs that run it refuse the Delivery, naming each changed switch and the plan revision that pins the new values, in order, until `approve-execution` re-pins the current policy and lists the changed fields in `refreshed_delivery_pins`; a policy that changes none of those values, one with every switch at its default included, agrees with a Delivery that pinned none. `process_policy.py value --delivery DLV-###`, task derivation and `delivery_compile.py`'s own switch reads refuse such a change of the switch they read instead of reading the new value. A switch no Delivery flow owns, such as `mechanical_pass_tier`, is no part of the pin and is read from the current policy inside a Delivery too. From the Delivery Review on, and for a merged or cancelled Delivery, the pin is kept as the record of what the Delivery ran under and its revision's values are read back, from the current policy or from Git history by the pinned source hash, so a policy set for the next Delivery never changes them; `value` then reports the commit that held the revision. Setup's project refresh declares the new `delivery.md` properties in `.obsidian/types.json`. `delivery_git.py reserve-delivery` and `publish-execution-plan` carry the pinned policy revision onto the Integration with the package, as publication carries a pinned Operation contract: the checkout's file when it is that revision, otherwise the approved file the Git history of the policy holds under the pinned source hash, so a later revision that sets every Delivery switch the same way never replaces it, and they refuse when neither holds it. `start-item` refreshes it in the Item, so an Item worktree holds the policy its Delivery pinned before the policy's own commit reaches the target, where every code review registration and evidence approval in it refused that the pinned policy no longer existed.
